GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2013-10-14T06:39:22Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: Consuming a DB created for Rails app
Description: I have decided to move some functionality of an existing Rails API into Node.js. I picked up Sequelize as an ORM mainly because it seemed like it is the most feature rich out of the many others.

So I started mapping my models from Rails in Sequelize (since I didn`t need all the columns I only mapped the necessary ones) and I ended up with a 1-n relationship that is done using :through in Rails. So I created the following ralationship:

```
Hole.hasMany(TrackingGroup, {foreignKey: 'hole_id', joinTableName:'holes_tracking_groups', underscored: true, useJunctionTable: true}); 

TrackingGroup.belongsTo(Hole, {foreignKey: 'tracking_group_id', joinTableName: 'holes_tracking_groups'});
```

The idea is that when I get all the tracking groups for a hole I will have a query in the holes_tracking_groups where the hole_id = "something" but instead I was having a query in the tracking_group table (the one that has all the tracking groups). Or in other words the specified joinTableName was not considered at all.

llm_response:
CATEGORY: 1
REASONING: This issue is about a conceptual misunderstanding of how to set up relationships in Sequelize ORM when working with an existing Rails database. The problem involves incorrect configuration of a many-to-many relationship using a join table. This is purely a code configuration issue that can be analyzed without needing to build or run the code. An LLM can verify that the relationship setup is incorrect (the parameters in the belongsTo method don't match what's needed for a join table relationship) and suggest the proper Sequelize syntax for handling a "through" relationship. No build environment is needed to understand the issue or verify a solution - it's simply about correcting the Sequelize model definitions to properly use the join table.
